paper.title: Statler: State-Maintaining Language Models for Embodied Reasoning
paper.central_claim: Explicit estimated world state maintained by prompted world-state writer and consulted by a world-state reader improves long-horizon embodied reasoning and sequential task success over implicit-history LLM robot policies.

signatures.object: Sequential tabletop world state and robot action code
signatures.information: User query, task-specific few-shot demonstrations, explicit JSON estimated state; hidden cleanliness/weight inferred from instructions/history, real positions via RealSense/MDETR
signatures.operation: Reader emits Python action plus update_wm call; writer predicts next JSON state from query/action and previous state; save state and supply it to next reader call
signatures.output: Executed primitive program and persistent within-episode state estimate
signatures.conditions: Correct update semantics and reader use of current state; world changes/action outcomes must be represented accurately
signatures.feedback: State is model-estimated, not a sound simulator transition or automatic truth reconciliation; subsequent queries carry new observations/information
signatures.selection_rule: Generated state replaces/updates prior state without measured independent acceptance gate
signatures.data: Task/domain few-shot query-code/state examples; evaluation20 episodes/domain, real10 episodes
signatures.persistence: JSON state within query sequence; not improved model weights, learned reusable skill or accepted cross-task harness edit
signatures.later_use: Next query conditions on current estimated state, rather than relying only on long history
signatures.claimed_effect: Correctly track latent temporal relations and reduce history-based reasoning failures
signatures.failure_boundary: Writer hallucination corrupts future state; reader may misreason correct state; context and prompt sensitivity; exact prompt sequences omitted

gap.author_gap: Implicit history-only LLM reasoning fails to track changing state over long-horizon tasks, including latent cleanliness, relative weight and occlusion.
gap.checked_gap: Explicit state is a concrete response to temporal-query degradation, tested against CaP and CoT; near-perfect non-temporal versus poor temporal CaP accuracy is useful diagnostic evidence but truncated-prefix denominators prevent a clean paired step-effect estimate.

gap.closest_adjacent: CaP and CaP+CoT local controls; state maintenance is contrasted with implicit histories, not an exact symbolic belief-state solver.

gap.stakes: Temporal errors compound across queries, including semantic variables invisible to current camera input.
gap.method_response: Externalize current state and update it at explicit action boundaries instead of asking every call to reconstruct full history.
gap.remaining_gap: Error-correcting state grounding, exact prompt reproducibility, fair token/turn budgets, distribution-shift holdouts and physical robustness remain open.

claims.text: Explicit state improves long-horizon robot task reasoning over CaP/CoT.
claims.setting: Three simulated tabletop domains with task-conditioned prompts;20 episodes/domain
claims.baseline/control: CaP, CaP+CoT; state/no-state, unified and automatic-instruction writer
claims.selection_vs_test: Selected challenging query episodes; precise prompt-development/test overlap cannot be fully audited without omitted full prompts
claims.result/denominator: Episode SR.50/.40/.55 vsCaP0/0/0; CoT.25/0/.30 with disinfection context overflow. Step SR.88/.82/.93. Step-type prefixes have unequal denominators due stopping.
counterevidence: Auto episode.75/.45/.40 beats standard.50/.40/.55 on first2 domains; no evidence standard uniformly best.
Conditional-prefix step accuracy is not paired unconditional success.
claims.allowed_conclusion: On this selected three-domain suite, explicit state is associated with substantially better completed episodes; no universal best prompting design or broad generalization.

claims.text: State maintenance benefits real robot manipulation.
claims.baseline/control: CaP; same domain/API but no matched full token/call cost
